correctness.rationale: For all r,s>=2 the subset-to-nucleus representation is a verified finite-poset theorem. The top and bottom action formulas are obtained directly by evaluating each upper cone. Their two-case composition comparison establishes both implications of the commuting criterion using arbitrary top upsets as separating inputs. Two different perfect matchings of an alleged cycle would be distinct increasing bijections of the same finite chains, impossible; thus any commuting family gives a forest and the sharp bound. For equality the incomparability graph on nonempty proper lower subsets is connected, forcing a common top leaf and then one of the two Boolean endpoints, yielding exactly the explicit two largest families. The ordered-pair formula follows from equal/comparable/incomparable bottom subsets. Its diagonal asymptotic follows from an exact four-exponential expression. Standalone code directly checks all nucleus identities, commutation and maximum cliques for four small parameter pairs; no finite run substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2021 Ochs paper and foundational 2014 Lindenhovius paper provide the subset-to-nucleus bijection but neither gives a two-Boolean-level commutation graph, a no-cycle structural lemma, a maximum pairwise-commuting family classification, or a pair count. Hemelaer examines cardinalities of topologies and Escardo examines composition/joins of nuclei, not these finite extremal and probabilistic invariants. Similarity discovery found no directly covering claim. A prior one-root star result has a single lower vertex, and its formula does not imply the new r>=2 incomparable-bottom constraints, forest bound, or exactly two extremizers. No stronger published implication was identified in inspected material; novelty is a supported self-review conclusion subject to residual bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier semigroup or locale literature may express an equivalent extremal commutation-graph theorem without the words nuclei or Heyting.
The full 79-page Lindenhovius paper was inspected at the relevant theorem and surrounding definitions, not line-by-line in unrelated chapters.
Database similarity ranking and unsuccessful keyword searches cannot establish global uniqueness.

value.rationale: Order-independent composition of nuclei is a natural compatibility invariant in finite intuitionistic/locale semantics. The theorem resolves both an extremal structural question (largest compatible collections and uniquely two extremizers) and a two-parameter probabilistic one (exact commuting-pair counts, with exponential decay in the balanced regime). The forest lemma gives a reusable structural mechanism rather than a direct substitution or re-count of nuclei. Prior one-root formulas cannot capture incomparable lower subsets for r>=2. The exact constants and equality cases are intrinsic, not arbitrary slices; the result is not claimed for higher levels or for all maximal families.
